note: Refreshed every week by the program's research task. Each item says what changed, why it matters to a data engineer or architect, and how to test the claim yourself.

items.title: Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI was hijacked to steal cloud and CI credentials
items.summary: On 17 November 2026 two malicious releases, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, of Microsoft's Agent Framework Python package were published to PyPI. A .pth file ran a credential stealer at Python start-up, even without an import, looking for Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face and OpenAI secrets and asking for Azure managed identity and CI OIDC tokens. PyPI quarantined both within minutes; 1.26.0 is the clean release.
items.why: Agent frameworks run where the keys are: next to warehouse credentials, CI tokens and model API keys. An architect pins exact versions with hashes, installs agents in a sandbox with only the secrets that task needs, and treats a new release of an agent library like a new database driver: reviewed before it reaches a pipeline.
items.try: In projects/ai-foundations, pin requirements.txt with hashes (pip-compile --generate-hashes or pip hash) and run lab1_loop.py with only the one environment variable it needs; list every other secret the process could read and how you would remove it.

items.title: dbt Charts answers questions with charts inside Claude and ChatGPT through an MCP server (beta)
items.summary: dbt Labs' November update makes dbt Charts available in Claude and ChatGPT through an MCP server (beta), drawing on the dbt semantic layer; dbt reports 20 to 50% fewer tokens than having the assistant build a dashboard from scratch, on its own benchmark. dbt State gets a free plan and Beta cost attribution tables on Snowflake.
items.why: The chat assistant is becoming a front end for the governed metric layer. The architect's job is to make sure the MCP tool can only read certified metrics, so the chart in a chat window matches the dashboard, and to measure the token saving on your own questions rather than the vendor's.
items.try: Extend labs/lab9_mcp_server.py with a fourth tool, get_metric(name, grain), that only answers from a fixed list of certified SQL definitions, then compare tokens per answer in lab5_evals.py against letting the agent write the SQL with run_sql.

items.title: Claude computer use reaches Team and Enterprise plans (beta)
items.summary: From 20 November 2026, Claude's computer use is available in beta on Team and Enterprise plans, in the new Claude Desktop experience and on web and mobile where Computer access is turned on by an admin. It is rolling out gradually.
items.why: An agent that drives screens reaches the tools that have no API: old BI tools, vendor consoles, admin pages. That is also the least auditable path. Prefer an API or MCP tool, keep screen control for read-only checks, and make sure an admin decides which teams can turn it on.
items.try: In lab10_oncall.py, list each action the on-call agent takes and mark whether it has an API or tool path or would need screen control; for every screen-only action, write the approval step and the audit line you would require.

items.title: Claude API: linked billing lets your customers pay for the Claude usage in your app (beta)
items.summary: Since 17 November 2026, an app built on the Claude API can bill a customer's own Claude organization for the usage it causes, with a beta header and a billing_policy field on the Messages request. Customers set spend caps or unlink in the Console; it works only where the customer's organization pays Anthropic directly.
items.why: Who pays for tokens becomes a per-request decision, not a contract clause. For an internal data platform the same idea is showback: tag every model call with the team that caused it, so cost per successful task can be charged back and capped per team.
items.try: Add a team field to each call in harness/trace.py, run lab7_optimise.py for two pretend teams, and report tokens and cost per team and per successful task; set a cap and show the run that would be refused.

items.title: Claude's text watermark now covers Opus 4.6, Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and Haiku 4.5
items.summary: Since 16 November 2026 the text watermark applies to more Claude models on supported platforms. Requests that set a non-default temperature, top_p or top_k may come back without it. A beta organization webhook also reports when a customer-managed encryption key fails or recovers.
items.why: When LLM output lands in tables (summaries, extracted fields, generated docs), provenance matters for audit and for training data later. Do not rely on a watermark alone: store the model, prompt version and request id beside every generated column, and alert on the key events that would stop the pipeline.
items.try: In lab3_prompts.py, write each generated answer to DuckDB with model, prompt hash, sampling settings and request id columns, then query which rows would be missing a watermark because of their sampling settings.
